items.title: How failure to destroy juvenile crime records is hurting children’s rehabilitation
items.summary: In India, recruitment drives for the armed forces, central paramilitary forces, and state police organisations often see qualified candidates suddenly disqualified during background checks. In most instances, the issue is not an adult criminal record but rather a childhood infraction that comes to light and derails their careers before they even begin. In one such case I worked on, a candidate cleared the recruitment process and joined constable training in a Central Armed Police Force (CAPF). After joining, he was required to fill out a verification form revealing his criminal antecedents. He bonafidely omitted the details, as the record was old and related to him as a minor. Eventually, during the candidate antecedent check, authorities discovered he was involved in a street scuffle as a minor and faced a criminal charge. Consequently, the recruiting authority cancelled his appointment because a criminal case was registered against him in the past. For youths from rural and working-class backgrounds, uniformed jobs are not simply employment but a pillar for them and their families to gain social leverage, protection and class mobility in their societies. Union of India & Ors.]. The petition, filed through the State Commissioner of Food Safety, asserts that the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 (FSSA) aims to decentralise food regulation. Under the Act, licensing and enforcement powers belong to State Commissioners and their designated officers. It specifically challenges the 2011 Licensing Regulations, the 2018 Recruitment Regulations, and the 2026 Amendment Regulations. According to the plea, the FSSAI Chief Executive Officer (CEO) exercised powers unlawfully by creating posts like ‘Central Food Safety Officer’ and ‘Central Licensing Authority’. items.title: Judicial delays and a new (ab)normal of unsaid restraint on freedom of judicial expression

Union of India , challenging the constitutional validity of the Chief Election Commissioner and other Election Commissioners (Appointment, Conditions of Service and Term of Office) Act, 2023 , has reignited debate around several contentious issues ranging from judges appointing judges, the procedural fairness and propriety of a belated preliminary objection seeking a Constitution Bench, judicial propriety concerning another judge on the Bench and the role of the Chief Justice as Master of the Roster. Yet, beneath these questions lies a more subtle institutional concern: whether judicial delay has begun to affect not merely the delivery of justice to litigants, but also the practical consequences of disagreement between Judges, where judicial freedom of expression can become practically inconsequential despite being expressed in strong and reasoned terms. items.summary: The Central Consumer Protection Authority (CCPA) has imposed a penalty of ₹1 lakh on Britannia Industries Limited for misleading consumers by advertising bread containing only 62% whole wheat flour as "100% Whole Wheat Bread." In an order dated October 21, Chief Commissioner Nidhi Khare and Commissioner Anupam Mishra held that the company's packaging and advertisements falsely conveyed that the bread was made entirely from whole wheat flour. " The Opposite Party has not merely overstated the proportion of whole wheat in the impugned product but has also employed a product nomenclature that is, on the stated facts, inconsistent with the prescribed compositional requirement ," the CCPA observed. The Authority directed Britannia to immediately discontinue the misleading advertisements and submit a compliance report within 15 days. The proceedings arose from the Authority's suo motu examination of Britannia's promotional claims, including "100% Whole Wheat Bread", "0% Maida" and statements describing its bread product as suitable for a healthy diet. items.title: Bengaluru Police arrest Bihar man over AI-generated Vidhana Soudha bomb blast video
items.summary: The Bengaluru Police have arrested a 25-year-old man from Bihar for posting an AI-generated video showing a bomb blast at Vidhana Soudha, the seat of the Karnataka government. The accused, identified as Hazrath Ali Shoiab, is a native of Bihar’s Araria district and had been working as a daily-wage pipe fitter in Bengaluru for the past few months, police said. The FIR invokes Sections 353(1)(b) and 353(2) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS). Section 353(1)(b) penalises false information likely to cause public fear or alarm that could lead to an offence against the State or public tranquillity, while Section 353(2) covers false information likely to promote enmity or ill will between groups. Both provisions carry a punishment of up to three years in prison, a fine, or both. According to the complaint filed by a police inspector at Vidhana Soudha police station, the video was detected during social media monitoring at 9.26 am on October 20. It was posted on an Instagram account named jnx_king_h_g with the caption “Vidhanasabha Uda Diya Bam se” (Vidhana Soudha was blown up with a bomb). items.title: Saurav Ganguly moves Delhi High Court against movie Doosra, claims rights over Lord's shirtless celebration
items.summary: The Delhi High Court on Thursday refused to pass any order on a plea by former India cricket captain Sourav Ganguly’s plea to stay the release of the film “Doosra”. Justice Dinesh Bhatt said the case will be heard tomorrow (Thursday). The movie is scheduled to be released in theatres tomorrow. Justice Bhatt made it clear that he has not stopped the release of the film in theatres. "I have said no stay, so the film can go on," Justice Bhatt said. Ganguly and film production house Luv Films LLP have approached the Delhi High Court seeking to restrain the release of the film citing exploitation of the former's life events, particularly his captaincy in the NatWest cricket series final and his shirtless celebration at Lord's. They have alleged unauthorised commercial exploitation of Ganguly’s personality rights and infringement of the production house’s exclusive contractual rights over his proposed biopic.
